$note: Hand-written smoke exercises so runtimes, the exercise screen, and the e2e flows have real rows from Phase 0. One per browser runtime plus Java. Function tests: input is a JSON array of arguments, expected is the JSON-serialized return value.

exercises.title: First late train
exercises.prompt:
A station logs the minutes past the hour at which trains arrived. A train is late if it arrived after the limit.

Write `first_late(times, limit)` that returns the first arrival time that is greater than `limit`. If no train is late, return `-1`.

Example: `first_late([3, 5, 9], 6)` returns `9`. `first_late([1, 2], 10)` returns `-1`.

exercises.title: Username check
exercises.prompt:
A sign-up form accepts a username. Write `validateUsername(name)` that returns `"ok"` when the name is 3 to 12 characters long and contains only lowercase letters or digits. Otherwise return the first problem found, in this order: `"too short"`, `"too long"`, `"bad characters"`.

Example: `validateUsername("ali7")` returns `"ok"`. `validateUsername("Al")` returns `"too short"`.

exercises.title: Orders per city
exercises.prompt:
A shop stores customers and their orders. Write one query that returns each city with the number of orders placed by customers from that city, as columns `city` and `order_count`, ordered by `order_count` descending then `city` ascending. Cities with zero orders must still appear.

Tables: `customers(id, name, city)` and `orders(id, customer_id, amount)`.

tests.input: select city, count(o.id) as order_count from customers c left join orders o on o.customer_id = c.id group by city order by order_count desc, city asc
tests.name: example

exercises.referenceSolution:
select c.city, count(o.id) as order_count
from customers c
left join orders o on o.customer_id = c.id
group by c.city
order by order_count desc, c.city asc;

exercises.title: Counter button
exercises.prompt:
The page has a button with id `inc` and a paragraph with id `count` showing `0`. Write the script so that each click on the button increases the number in the paragraph by one.

Example: after three clicks the paragraph shows `3`.

exercises.title: Shapes report
exercises.prompt:
Complete the class `Solution` with a static method `String describe(String kind, double a)` that builds the right shape and returns its description. A `Circle` with radius `a` describes itself as `circle:<area rounded to 1 decimal>`; a `Square` with side `a` as `square:<area rounded to 1 decimal>`. Both must extend an abstract `Shape` with an abstract `area()` and a concrete `describe()` that does the formatting, so the subclasses only compute area. Unknown kinds return `unknown`.

Example: `describe("square", 2)` returns `square:4.0`.
